cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Tell Me Why
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal the motive behind a choice by offering small pieces of your own truth as bait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll find us a shorter route. I avoid my old office too, but why are we circling the station?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My former boss catches this train.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll take the next one. I told mine I'd become a novelist. What did you tell yours?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That I had a better offer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've carried the same blank notebook past mine for a year. Are we avoiding him because there wasn't a better offer?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 takes route control; A3 yields train timing while offering a career pretense as bait; A5 exposes failure to test the better-offer motive.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 boss explains circling; A3 later train uses that concern and B4 better offer gives A5 a precise suspicion.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants to avoid an encounter and B4 answers narrowly, leaving A to risk a further disclosure.

heightening.evidence: A5 blank notebook turns a nominal career story into evidence of A own shame before the sharper question.

specificity.evidence: A1 station route and old office, B2 former boss and B4 claimed offer establish the immediate avoidance.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 notebook detail does work as disclosure; the final question tests one motive rather than explaining the game.
